title: Frontend entry systemdesign component library
question: You're asked to set up a simple shared component library (buttons, inputs, cards) that multiple pages in the same app will use. How would you structure it?
idealAnswer:
Each component should expose a small, clear set of props (e.g. variant, size, disabled) rather than letting callers pass arbitrary styles, to keep usage consistent

Shared design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) should live in one place and be consumed by all components, instead of hardcoded values duplicated per component

Components should be composable, e.g. a Button should work standalone or inside a Form, without hidden dependencies on where it's rendered

Include sensible accessible defaults (focus states, keyboard handling, ARIA attributes) baked into the components themselves so every consumer gets them for free

Some form of living documentation or preview (like Storybook) so other developers can discover what components exist and how to use them, rather than reading source code

Plan a versioning or update story from the start, so changing a shared Button doesn't silently break every page that uses it
